To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electronics is capable of delivering the desired dynamic range, noise level, and uniformity of shaping and gain over 64 channels, with a differential timing resolution between channels better than 1.4 ns at 1.2% of the dynamic scale.

the configurable shaper/digitizers for APD-based photon detectors have been successfully implemented with a dynamic range of 12 bits, an average RMS noise of 0.2 ADC counts, a linearity better than 1% and a uniformity of 2%.
the configurable electronics with low noise, wide dynamic range, and high uniformity is suitable for the readout of photon detectors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a low-noise, configurable, 14-bit dynamic, 32-channel shapers for APD readout in high-energy physics experiments.
the development of a new type of configurable shaper and digitizer electronics for photodiode based photon detectors.
the development of a configurable FEE with low noise and high dynamic range for the ALICE PHOS and EMCal detectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FEE design is well-suited for a wide range of applications with APDs, and is particularly well adapted for the ALICE PHOS and EMCal calorimeters.
the electronics has proven to be an excellent choice for ALICE and other applications.
the electronics presented here has been successfully adopted in ALICE for the two calorimeters PHOS and EMCal with APD readout and has been found to meet the design specifications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electronics has met all the design specifications and the requirements for the ALICE detectors.
we have developed a low-noise configurable electronics for photodiode based photon detectors with excellent performance.

we have developed and produced a configurable 32-channel electronics system that provides excellent noise performance, gain and timing uniformity, and a large dynamic range, which is essential for the operation of the APD-based PHOS detector of ALICE.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a low noise 14-bit digitizer can be implemented in a small and cost effective form factor with discrete logic.

it is possible to build a configurable, low-noise and low-cost shaper/digitiser with a large dynamic range and a wide range of shaping time, using discrete components on a multi-layer printed circuit board.
the design principles and the performance of the FEE card are well suited for other detector types with low noise and large dynamic range.
